identity.title: Prove canonical governance parity across EverRun-derived and second-producer fixtures

human_pressure.one_screen_brief: Use the existing generic MCP-style second-producer fixture and the post-fix EverRun-derived fixture to prove both travel through the same validator/load/ingest/projection/report/regression surfaces without producer-specific semantics. Compare structure and invariant behavior, not business outcomes that differ by evidence.
human_pressure.why_now: No Framework Left Behind must remain an executable property after EverRun dogfood hardens the canonical path.
red_lines: No forced identical business outcome across different evidence.

machine_core.goal: Extend existing second-producer conformance evidence so both canonical fixtures exercise shared package, projection, governed-result and regression read-model paths with producer identity semantically inert.
invariants: Different evidence may produce different governance outcomes.
Changing producer identity alone must not change normalized governance interpretation.
Unknown producer-private events remain preserved as evidence and do not create clean facts.

steps.title: Run both fixtures through shared pipeline
details: Validate/load/ingest/rebuild/report each fixture with identical function paths.

steps.title: Prove identity inertness
details: Clone normalized projections with source labels changed only and prove regression interpretation is unchanged.

steps.title: Prove unknown preservation
details: Confirm producer-private unknown events survive ingestion without being promoted into canonical clean facts.

acceptance: Both fixtures pass the same canonical path.
Producer identity alone does not affect projection/regression semantics.
Different evidence remains free to produce different outcomes.

producer.artifact: second-producer conformance evidence exercising shared package, projection, governed-result and regression paths

observable_effect.assertion: Both canonical fixtures exercise the same shared code paths without producer-specific branching.

proofs.assertion: Second-producer tests pass on shared production paths.

must_check: 8070/8071 fixture path is available and existing second-producer fixture remains valid.
Parity means shared semantics, not identical outcomes.
No production source-specific branches are introduced.
reject_if: Tests assert different producers must have identical governed outcomes despite different evidence.
A new adapter or producer-specific ontology is introduced.
Unknown events are dropped to reduce warnings.
